auth_module_map.role: Defines AbstractBaseUser (line 43) and BaseUserManager (line 21); provides password hashing, last_login, session auth hash, and USERNAME_FIELD contract — the minimal user contract for custom models

Defines PermissionsMixin (line 322, adds is_superuser/groups/user_permissions), AbstractUser (line 451, full-featured subclass of AbstractBaseUser+PermissionsMixin), concrete User (line 522, swappable via AUTH_USER_MODEL), and update_last_login signal receiver (line 18)

AuthConfig.ready() (line 18) wires post_migrate signals for permission creation and conditionally connects update_last_login only when last_login is a model field (line 27-32); registers check_user_model system check
Initial migration creating Permission, Group, and User tables; establishes migration dependency graph for apps that depend on auth
check_user_model validates custom user model compliance: requires USERNAME_FIELD, REQUIRED_FIELDS, and that the swapped model satisfies the AbstractBaseUser contract

migration_trace: STEP 1 — Audit existing fields: AbstractBaseUser (base_user.py:43-45) provides only `password` and `last_login`; AbstractUser (models.py:451) adds `username`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `email`, `is_staff`, `is_active`, `date_joined`; PermissionsMixin (models.py:322) adds `is_superuser`, `groups`, `user_permissions`. All of these map cleanly; the three custom fields do not.

STEP 2 — Rewrite the custom model to extend AbstractBaseUser (base_user.py:43) + PermissionsMixin (models.py:322) instead of AbstractUser. Re-declare any AbstractUser fields you want to keep (username, email, is_staff, etc.) directly on the model — AbstractBaseUser does not include them automatically.

STEP 3 — Implement mandatory AbstractBaseUser contract: set USERNAME_FIELD (base_user.py:69 calls getattr(self, self.USERNAME_FIELD)), set REQUIRED_FIELDS (base_user.py:49), and implement get_full_name()/get_short_name() if admin integration is needed (AbstractUser implements these at models.py:506-515).

STEP 4 — Create a custom manager subclassing BaseUserManager (base_user.py:21), implementing create_user() and create_superuser() with your extra required fields (profile_tier, etc.). Mirror the pattern in UserManager (models.py:145-217).

STEP 5 — Retain all three custom fields verbatim on the new AbstractBaseUser subclass (they have no auth equivalent — see unmappable_fields section). Add them after the inherited fields in the model definition.

STEP 6 — Set AUTH_USER_MODEL = 'yourapp.CustomUser' in settings.py. The swappable marker is declared on the concrete User model at models.py:531 (`swappable = 'AUTH_USER_MODEL'`); your custom model replaces it, so any ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL) references remain valid.

STEP 7 — Generate the squashed migration: run `makemigrations --name replace_abstractuser_with_abstractbaseuser`. Django's migration framework will detect the schema diff (dropped AbstractUser fields you choose not to keep, kept custom fields). The migration depends on auth (see 0001_initial.py:8 dependency pattern).

STEP 8 — Verify the system check passes: AuthConfig.ready() registers check_user_model (apps.py:33) which validates USERNAME_FIELD uniqueness, REQUIRED_FIELDS excludes USERNAME_FIELD, and no clashes in the permission-related M2M fields. Run `manage.py check --tag models`.

STEP 9 — Confirm update_last_login signal wiring: apps.py:27-32 only connects the signal when last_login is a DeferredAttribute (i.e., a real model field). Since AbstractBaseUser still declares last_login (base_user.py:45), this wires automatically — no manual signal connect needed.

STEP 10 — Data migration: write a RunPython migration operation to backfill any existing rows. profile_tier can default to 'free', external_sso_id can remain null (nullable=True), last_sync_at can remain null. Apply and verify with `migrate --plan`.

unmappable_fields.reason: Neither AbstractBaseUser (base_user.py:43-164) nor AbstractUser (models.py:451-519) nor PermissionsMixin (models.py:322-448) define any field representing subscription tier, account plan, or user classification. The auth framework models identity and permission, not business-tier metadata.
unmappable_fields.migration_strategy: Declare profile_tier = models.CharField(max_length=20, choices=[('free','Free'),('pro','Pro'),('enterprise','Enterprise')], default='free') directly on the new AbstractBaseUser subclass. It is a pure application-domain field and requires no auth wiring. Include a RunPython data migration to backfill 'free' for any null rows created during the schema transition.
unmappable_fields.evidence: django/contrib/auth/models.py:451-519 (AbstractUser field list contains no tier/plan concept); django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:43-45 (AbstractBaseUser has only password and last_login)

unmappable_fields.reason: AbstractBaseUser has a USERNAME_FIELD contract (base_user.py:69) and BaseUserManager.get_by_natural_key() (base_user.py:36) keyed to it, but these are for the primary login identifier. external_sso_id is a secondary, nullable external reference — auth has no field for federated identity tokens or SSO subject identifiers. Using USERNAME_FIELD for this would break normal username-based lookups.
unmappable_fields.migration_strategy: Keep external_sso_id = models.CharField(max_length=255, unique=True, null=True, blank=True) on the custom model. For SSO authentication, implement a custom authentication backend (subclass django.contrib.auth.backends.ModelBackend) that performs lookup by external_sso_id; wire it in AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS. The unique constraint is preserved at the DB level; no auth migration file needs changing.
unmappable_fields.evidence: django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:36-40 (get_by_natural_key uses USERNAME_FIELD only, no secondary ID slot); django/contrib/auth/backends.py provides ModelBackend as the extension point for custom lookup logic

unmappable_fields.reason: AbstractBaseUser defines last_login = models.DateTimeField(null=True) (base_user.py:45) which is superficially similar (a nullable DateTimeField), but it is semantically reserved for authentication events and is automatically updated by the update_last_login signal receiver (models.py:18-24) connected in apps.py:30-32. Reusing last_login for external-sync timestamps would corrupt auth session management and trigger incorrect session invalidation via get_session_auth_hash (base_user.py:132-149).
unmappable_fields.migration_strategy: Retain last_sync_at = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True) as a separate field on the custom model alongside the inherited last_login. Update it explicitly in your SSO sync service code, never via auth signals. This cleanly separates auth-event tracking (last_login, managed by Django at models.py:18-24) from sync-event tracking (last_sync_at, managed by application logic).
unmappable_fields.evidence: django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:45 (last_login definition); django/contrib/auth/models.py:18-24 (update_last_login signal receiver); django/contrib/auth/apps.py:27-32 (auto-connection of update_last_login on login signal)
